snippet.title: If The Grid Fails Tomorrow, Do You Have These 5 Items?
snippet.description:
When the power grid fails, most people make a massive, expensive mistake: they rush to the grocery store to panic-buy milk, bread, and eggs. But when the electricity is out for days, your refrigerator becomes a dark box and that food will rot in 48 hours.

True survival isn't about hoarding perishable groceries—it's about addressing the 5 mechanical failure points of your home before the blackout hits. Whether you are facing a severe winter ice storm, a cyber attack, or a blown transformer, your home is on a 24-hour countdown until it gets cold, dark, and potentially hazardous.

In this video, we break down the exact emergency loadout every home needs to survive a prolonged grid failure. We also dive into brilliant survival hacks straight from the preparedness community—like how to tap into your hot water heater for 50 gallons of emergency water if you don't have a bathtub!

🚨 IN THIS VIDEO, YOU WILL LEARN:
The Sanitation Crisis (Bathtub Bladders): Why securing up to 100 gallons of water isn't just for drinking, but for manually flushing toilets to prevent your home from becoming a biological hazard. (Plus, the "No-Bathtub" Hot Water Heater Hack!)
Hands-Free Lighting: Why LED Headlamps beat flashlights for operational efficiency, and the safest "Wet Sand Glass Jar" method if you absolutely must use candles.
The Cold Weather Defense: How to safely use an indoor propane heater with a built-in oxygen depletion sensor—and why you must pair it with a separate Carbon Monoxide (CO) monitor. (Live in a hot climate like South Florida? We cover the battery-powered fan strategy too!)
Silent Power Stations: The massive superiority of silent, fume-free Lithium Iron Phosphate (LiFePO4) solar generators over loud, target-painting gas generators.
The Psychological Blackout: Why a hand-crank NOAA weather radio is your ultimate defense against the intense anxiety of the 72-hour information vacuum.

🛑 STOP PANIC BUYING. START PREPARING SMART. The grid is a machine, and machines break. Stop buying things that rot, and start buying things that rescue.

snippet.title: Amid high temperatures, Department of Energy issues emergency order for electric grid
snippet.description:
In the midst of the heat wave, as temperatures rise, so do the concerns about Maryland's electric grid. With increasing demand and supply that isn't keeping up, the Department of Energy just issued an order allowing data centers and other large load customers to use back-up generation.

Earlier this week, in a request to the DOE, Michael Bryson, the Senior Vice President of Operations for PJM Interconnection - the regional grid representing 13 states and D.C. said, "the forecasted demand raises a significant risk of emergency conditions that could jeopardize electric reliability and public safety."

snippet.title: Tinubu Defends INEC+ Sowore Parades ‘Tinubu Must Go Bag’+ ADC Warns Tinubu Over El-Rufai| OjyOkpe
snippet.description:
A high-powered delegation of Catholic bishops led by Archbishop Ndagoso stormed Aso Rock to voice grave concerns over devastating northern security crises, grinding poverty, and the credibility of the 2027 polls, triggering a fierce national debate after President Tinubu stoutly defended INEC's impartiality.

Human rights lawyer Chidi Odinkalu sharply criticized the president's defense as a Kiss of Judas, arguing that a truly independent electoral commission should never require presidential certification to prove its integrity.

Meanwhile, former Vice President Atiku Abubakar declared that the 2027 elections must be decided strictly at the ballot box rather than in courtrooms, coming right after the Court of Appeal unanimously nullified the deregistration of the ADC and four other political parties.

In Kaduna, Governor Uba Sani won widespread praise after nominating accomplished tax administrator Jerry Adams as his 2027 running mate to promote inclusion, while AAC candidate Omoyele Sowore staged a bold protest at the Federal High Court in Abuja with a Ghana Must Go bag demanding that the current administration step down.

In Delta State, the APC strongly denied reports of chaos at its Effurun stakeholders' meeting attended by Aviation Minister Festus Keyamo, threatening legal action against a national newspaper despite viral videos showing a senior aide to Governor Sheriff Oborevwori being severely beaten.

Tragedy struck Plateau State as public outrage erupted over the brutal torture and murder of 25-year-old University of Jos graduate Ibrahim Mbaya, who was beaten to death by a mob over a missing iPhone 12, prompting the police to arrest three suspects.

In Oyo State, Governor Seyi Makinde announced a major security boost with the delivery of two long-awaited aerial surveillance aircraft at the Ibadan airport to step up regional intelligence gathering.

Finally, in corporate and entertainment milestones, Halima Dangote revealed that billionaire Aliko Dangote plans to donate one-third of his massive $35 billion fortune to charity. 

A heartwarming viral video captured Anambra State Governor Charles Soludo dancing with his son Ozonna to the hit song Big Flex.

snippet.title: POV: You’re Prepping for Pregnancy
snippet.description:
Sources- PMID 35012532 
Marissa on TT 

Preparing for pregnancy by taking folic acid and eliminating alcohol and tobacco creates an optimal foundation for conception and healthy fetal development. While folic acid is crucial for the mother to prevent severe neural tube defects in early embryogenesis, paternal nutrition and lifestyle before conception are also vital. Alcohol, smoking, and inadequate nutrient levels harm paternal sperm quality, damaging DNA integrity and lowering fertility, while maternal exposure to alcohol and nicotine directly compromises early placental development and increases the risk of miscarriage or low birth weight. When both parents commit to these health changes several months prior to trying to conceive, they optimize the genetic material of both sperm and egg during their development window. Removing toxins from the domestic environment protects early cellular division from harmful chemical exposures before a pregnancy test even registers positive. Furthermore, adopting these lifestyle choices together fosters a supportive partnership, ensuring both partners share accountability in nurturing the healthiest possible start for their future child. 

#family #child #mother

We spent a year stockpiling a year's worth of food, and in this video we lay the whole lot out on the table and talk through exactly how we did it. This is bulk food buying and long term food storage on an Australian homestead, driven by a simple reality: the cost of living keeps climbing faster than wages, food prices keep rising, and food shortages keep turning up in the news. Our approach to food security has never been about doomsday or panic. It's about building a deep buffer that gives you options in any scenario, from a tight grocery week to a genuine supply disruption. If you've been thinking about emergency preparedness, prepper pantry basics, or simply getting ahead on your grocery budget, this is the practical, real-numbers walkthrough we wish we'd had when we started.

We cover what actually makes the cut for long term food storage (and what doesn't), our decision framework for what to buy in bulk, where we shop here in Australia (Honest to Goodness, Costco, our local wholesaler, and yes, sometimes just Coles and Woolworths), what it really cost us per 100g compared to supermarket prices, and how we store it all in drums, Mylar bags and our pantry system so it actually gets used. This is part of our ongoing series on self sufficiency, homesteading and practical independence for Australian families, so check the playlist for the full bulk food storage setup that came before this one, and grab our free downloadable bulk food guide (linked below) with everything we bought, where we bought it, and the storage method we use. snippet.title: Nationwide Blackout Alert; Nine Substation Failures Collapse ENTIRE Grid, Could Last 18 MONTHS
snippet.description:
- The United States is at risk of a nationwide blackout that could last 18 months, according to the former chairman of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.

Jon Wellinghoff became aware of the alleged vulnerability after a shooting at a Pacific Gas and Electric Company's San Jose substation, according to the The New York Times Magazine.

He conducted a power flow analysis that modeled the large-scale effects of knocking out the most critical substation in each of America's three power grids: the Western, Eastern and Texas interconnections. He said this led him to discover just how easy it would be to cripple America's power supply.

'We came up with some very astounding numbers,' Wellinghoff said. 'If you knock out nine total substations among these three grids, you can black out the entire United States.'

It does not matter which nine substations are taken offline either, he noted, as long as each one is among the 10 most important for its region.

Alternatively, bad actors could blackout the three interconnections individually.

'I mean, it's not like there are particular substations,' he explained. 'You just have to figure out what are the top 10 critical ones in each of those interconnects - which to do that, it's probably something that a bunch of 12 year olds with the Internet could do pretty easily.

'All you have to do is look at a map of the grid and figure out where most of the wires go into the substations - that's a critical substation.' 

Once he made that terrifying discovery, which came back in 2013, Wellinghoff briefed the White House, Congress and the Department of Energy.

'I basically wrote a memo about what happened and gave it to everybody I could to explain to them that we need to do something immediately,' he said.

It warned that a blackout caused by lost transformers could last 18 months or longer.

The Department of Homeland Security then sent a delegation around the country, urging utilities to increase security at their substations.

'We did a nationwide tour to alert owners and operators about the vulnerabilities,' said Caitlin Durkovich, the then-assistant secretary for infrastructure protection.

But with more than 200,000 miles of high-voltage transmission lines and roughly 55,000 substations scattered across the country, 'there is awareness that you can't protect everything.'

A year later, the North American Electric Reliability Corporation, an industry-led public-private entity charged with protecting the grid, published a 'reliability standard' for utilities. This required them to assess their substations and prepare a plan to defend them from physical attacks. 

How to do so was left to the utilities. 

If the United States were to experience a year-long blackout, the results would be catastrophic.

At first, critical infrastructure like sewage plants, water treatment plants and hospitals would be able to remain operational as long as they have enough diesel or natural gas. Those with emergency radios could also listen for updates from one of 73 Primary Entry Point Stations, which are supplied with 60 days of generator fuel.

But once the diesel ran out and natural gas pumps shut down, it would become more difficult to restore the grid, considering so many utilities rely on fossil fuels to 'black-start' their generating units.

At that point, 'the supply of food, water and fuel would degrade within days,' according to a 2010 report prepared by NERC and the Energy Department.

localized.title: Nationwide Blackout Alert; Nine Substation Failures Collapse ENTIRE Grid, Could Last 18 MONTHS
localized.description:
- The United States is at risk of a nationwide blackout that could last 18 months, according to the former chairman of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.

Jon Wellinghoff became aware of the alleged vulnerability after a shooting at a Pacific Gas and Electric Company's San Jose substation, according to the The New York Times Magazine.

He conducted a power flow analysis that modeled the large-scale effects of knocking out the most critical substation in each of America's three power grids: the Western, Eastern and Texas interconnections. He said this led him to discover just how easy it would be to cripple America's power supply.

'We came up with some very astounding numbers,' Wellinghoff said. 'If you knock out nine total substations among these three grids, you can black out the entire United States.'

It does not matter which nine substations are taken offline either, he noted, as long as each one is among the 10 most important for its region.

Alternatively, bad actors could blackout the three interconnections individually.

'I mean, it's not like there are particular substations,' he explained. 'You just have to figure out what are the top 10 critical ones in each of those interconnects - which to do that, it's probably something that a bunch of 12 year olds with the Internet could do pretty easily.

'All you have to do is look at a map of the grid and figure out where most of the wires go into the substations - that's a critical substation.' 

Once he made that terrifying discovery, which came back in 2013, Wellinghoff briefed the White House, Congress and the Department of Energy.

'I basically wrote a memo about what happened and gave it to everybody I could to explain to them that we need to do something immediately,' he said.

It warned that a blackout caused by lost transformers could last 18 months or longer.

The Department of Homeland Security then sent a delegation around the country, urging utilities to increase security at their substations.

'We did a nationwide tour to alert owners and operators about the vulnerabilities,' said Caitlin Durkovich, the then-assistant secretary for infrastructure protection.

But with more than 200,000 miles of high-voltage transmission lines and roughly 55,000 substations scattered across the country, 'there is awareness that you can't protect everything.'

A year later, the North American Electric Reliability Corporation, an industry-led public-private entity charged with protecting the grid, published a 'reliability standard' for utilities. This required them to assess their substations and prepare a plan to defend them from physical attacks. 

How to do so was left to the utilities. 

If the United States were to experience a year-long blackout, the results would be catastrophic.

At first, critical infrastructure like sewage plants, water treatment plants and hospitals would be able to remain operational as long as they have enough diesel or natural gas. Those with emergency radios could also listen for updates from one of 73 Primary Entry Point Stations, which are supplied with 60 days of generator fuel.

But once the diesel ran out and natural gas pumps shut down, it would become more difficult to restore the grid, considering so many utilities rely on fossil fuels to 'black-start' their generating units.

At that point, 'the supply of food, water and fuel would degrade within days,' according to a 2010 report prepared by NERC and the Energy Department.

It added that 'communication of information to the general population would be greatly complicated by the loss of cellphones, internet access and television' and 'the economy would virtually shut down as electronic transactions could no longer be processed.

'After several days, widespread social unrest and confusion would ensue.'

Back in March 2011, a 9.0-magnitude earthquake triggered a massive tsunami that claimed nearly 20,000 lives and caused a meltdown at Fukushima nuclear plant. Since then, Japan has invested heavily in tsunami prevention and preparedness.
